items.name: gSHAPE
items.tagline: Soil Health Assessment Protocol and Evaluation
items.description: A web tool for context-specific soil health assessment and benchmarking.
items.image_alt: gSHAPE interface with location, evaluation framework, and soil indicator selections
items.heading: Make soil measurements more meaningful.
paragraphs: A soil measurement needs context. gSHAPE offers a browser interface for exploring evaluation frameworks and measured indicators alongside the location and inputs relevant to the selected assessment.
It brings physical, chemical, and biological indicators into one place for soil health assessment and benchmarking.
items.steps_introduction: Use your measured data. Follow the tool’s field labels and units for the selected framework.

steps.title: Set the location
steps.description: Choose the country and complete any location fields requested by the tool.

steps.title: Select a framework
steps.description: Choose an available evaluation framework appropriate to your assessment.

steps.title: Choose indicators
steps.description: Select the soil indicators you have measured, then enter the requested values and units.

steps.title: Review the assessment
steps.description: Explore the scores and guidance shown by the tool. Interpret them within your soil and management context.

items.interface_description: The live app lets you choose a location, evaluation framework, and target soil health indicators.
items.caption: gSHAPE start screen, captured November 17, 2026. This is an interface example, not a soil assessment result.

indicators.title: Physical indicators
indicators.description: Examples in the interface include bulk density, macroaggregate stability, and available water capacity.

indicators.title: Chemical indicators
indicators.description: Examples include pH, soil phosphorus, extractable potassium, and electrical conductivity.

indicators.title: Biological indicators
indicators.description: Examples include soil organic carbon, potentially mineralizable nitrogen, and microbial biomass carbon.
